# Kronus Intelligence Group

> We build and operate protective intelligence: executive threat assessment, institutional threat monitoring, counterparty vetting, and narrative threat detection.

Kronus Intelligence Group (KIG) is a protective-intelligence firm founded by Adrienne Uthe. KIG scopes, builds, and operates intelligence capability for each client's environment, combining more than 30 years of field intelligence with analyst-led systems and network analysis. Client relationships are not published.

- Languages spoken natively: EN, AR (Levantine), HT, FR, ES, SR (six)
- Contact: project@kronusintelligencegroup.com
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/kronus-intelligence-group

## Insights

- [Red Flags in Due Diligence | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/red-flags-in-due-diligence): Standard due diligence checks what a counterparty discloses; private intelligence firms surface the undisclosed control and exposure it never catches.
- [Competitive Intelligence Firm | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/competitive-intelligence-firm): A competitive intelligence firm goes beyond monitoring competitors — it maps decision-makers, capabilities, and strategy shifts to anticipate what happens next.
- [Geopolitical Risk for Businesses | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/geopolitical-risk-for-businesses): Geopolitical risk creates direct operational exposure for businesses — disrupted supply chains, frozen assets, stranded personnel — not abstract headline risk.
- [How to Detect Disinformation Campaigns | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/how-to-detect-disinformation-campaigns): Detecting disinformation campaigns requires signal indicators, attribution methodology, and dedicated intelligence infrastructure, not reactive crisis response.
- [What Is Executive Protection Intelligence? | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/what-is-executive-protection-intelligence): Executive protection intelligence is the analytical layer that turns physical security decisions from reaction into an evidence-based, defensible process.
- [How to Vet a Business Partner | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/how-to-vet-a-business-partner): Vetting a business partner well means going past legal screening to surface undisclosed risk that incorporation records and credit checks never catch.
- [What Is Narrative Intelligence? | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/what-is-narrative-intelligence): Narrative intelligence is the structured collection and analysis of how damaging stories move and spread against organizations before the harm is visible.
- [HUMINT vs OSINT: Key Differences | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/humint-vs-osint): HUMINT and OSINT answer different intelligence requirements — effective programs choose based on the question at hand, not a fixed preference.
- [How Do Private Intelligence Firms Work? | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/how-do-private-intelligence-firms-work): Private intelligence firms operate as intelligence producers, not investigators or consultants, using structured tradecraft to answer specific client questions.
- [What Is Corporate OSINT? | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/corporate-osint): Corporate OSINT applies disciplined open source collection and analysis to counterparty risk, competitive insight, and due diligence, beyond a basic search.
- [Counterintelligence Consulting | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/counterintelligence-consulting): Counterintelligence consulting protects against threats cybersecurity cannot reach: insider recruitment, foreign penetration, and human sources already inside.
- [Field Intelligence Services | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/field-intelligence-services): Field intelligence services put analysts on the ground to answer questions desk research cannot, verifying facts no database alone can supply.
- [Pattern of Life Analysis Explained | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/pattern-of-life-analysis): Pattern of life analysis maps behavioral routines to detect meaningful deviations, supporting threat assessment, executive protection, and counterintelligence.
- [Executive Digital Footprint Reduction | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/executive-digital-footprint-reduction): Executive digital footprint reduction audits public records, data broker listings, and social exposure, then suppresses what makes leaders targetable.
- [Electoral Integrity Monitoring | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/electoral-integrity-monitoring): Electoral integrity monitoring combines OSINT, HUMINT, and narrative analysis to catch foreign interference and influence operations while still in motion.
- [Deepfake Detection Services | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/deepfake-detection-services): Deepfake detection services identify synthetic audio, video, and fabricated documents used in fraud, disinformation, and targeted deception operations.
- [TSCM Services: Countermeasures Explained | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/tscm-services): TSCM services detect and neutralize covert surveillance devices and electronic eavesdropping in conference rooms, offices, and communication systems.
- [What Is a Narrative Intelligence Firm? | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/narrative-intelligence-firm): A narrative intelligence firm catches damaging stories while they're still forming, giving organizations time to respond before reputational damage compounds.
- [What Is HUMINT Intelligence? | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/what-is-humint-intelligence): HUMINT intelligence is information gathered from human sources under defined tradecraft and legal constraints — a discipline no database can replicate.
- [AI Answer Poisoning: A New Narrative-Threat Vector | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/ai-answer-poisoning): Attackers seed fake support numbers and login pages into ChatGPT, Gemini and AI Overview answers. What the Dark Sourcery disclosure does and does not show.
- [Private Intelligence Firm vs. Security Firm | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/private-intelligence-firm-vs-security-firm): A private intelligence firm and a security firm answer different questions at different points in the threat timeline — conflating them leaves risk unaddressed.
- [Geopolitical Risk Assessment Framework | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/geopolitical-risk-assessment): A rigorous geopolitical risk assessment translates political instability into concrete operational exposure, beyond headline-driven risk-matrix scoring.
- [Disinformation Detection Explained | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/disinformation-detection): Disinformation detection requires structured frameworks and signal analysis to identify coordinated false narratives before they spread beyond containment.
- [What Is OSINT? Open Source Intelligence Explained | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/what-is-osint): OSINT, or open source intelligence, is the systematic collection and analysis of publicly available information to produce genuinely actionable intelligence.
- [Executive Threat Assessment Framework | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/executive-threat-assessment): Executive threat assessment identifies who actually poses a credible risk to senior leaders and why, using a practitioner framework, not guesswork.
- [Counterparty Vetting for High-Stakes Deals | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/counterparty-vetting): Counterparty vetting goes beyond standard due diligence, applying intelligence tradecraft to surface conduct and exposure legal review alone won't catch.
- [Corporate Intelligence Services | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/corporate-intelligence-services): Corporate intelligence services close the gap between what executives know and what counterparties, markets, and competitors are actually doing.
- [Narrative Threat Monitoring | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/narrative-threat-monitoring): Narrative threat monitoring tracks how damaging stories about an organization form and spread, catching them before they escalate into an uncontainable crisis.
- [HUMINT Services Explained | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/humint-services): HUMINT services deliver intelligence sourced from human networks — information that no database, algorithm, or public record can reach on its own.
- [What Is a Private Intelligence Firm? | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/what-is-a-private-intelligence-firm): A private intelligence firm collects, analyzes, and delivers actionable intelligence for clients who cannot rely on governments or public information alone.
- [The €95M Fideuram Deepfake Voice Fraud | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/fideuram-deepfake-voice-fraud): A cloned voice and a spoofed WhatsApp moved roughly €95M out of an Intesa Sanpaolo unit. What is established, and why executive impersonation is an exposure problem.
- [AI Attack Ads in the Midterms: Preparing for Deepfakes | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/ai-attack-ads-midterms-deepfake-disclosure): Axios reported on October 19 that 220 AI-generated ads have aired in the midterms, with no federal disclosure rule. How a named person or brand should prepare.
- [Cloned News Sites Built to Be Cited by AI Assistants | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/cloned-news-sites-ai-assistant-citation-risk): Alethea reported on October 16 that a Russia-linked network routed readers to cloned news sites, some indexed by Google. Why AI assistants raise the stakes.
- [Fake News Clips in Borrowed Outlet Branding | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/fake-news-clips-matryoshka-midterms): Russia, Iran and China-linked networks use generative AI for fake videos, fake journalists and clips styled as real outlets. How organizations should prepare.
- [Asos Breach: When Attackers Set the Disclosure Clock | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/asos-breach-disclosure-clock): Asos hackers impersonated a trusted contact, hijacked the app's push channel and contacted the BBC while the first statement understated the data taken.
- [Colorado's First Deepfake Disclosure Case | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/colorado-deepfake-disclosure-case): Colorado's Secretary of State filed what appears to be the first complaint under a state deepfake disclosure law. What is alleged and contested, and what to do.
- [OpenAI's False-Front Influence Operations | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/openai-false-front-influence-operations): OpenAI reports a Russian fake think tank and an Iranian network of seven invented journalists placed stories in real media. What is established, what to check.
- [Deepfake Readiness Gap: Pindrop's 2026 Survey | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/deepfake-readiness-gap-pindrop-2026): Pindrop's 2026 survey of 250 US security leaders finds 74% saw or suspected a deepfake attack and 10% have purpose-built tools. What it shows, and its limits.
- [Impersonation Phishing Targets AI Policy Experts: TA419 | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/ta419-ai-policy-impersonation): Proofpoint says a China-aligned group posed as a former White House official, an economist and an Anthropic employee to target AI policy experts.
- [AI Influence Operations: Capacity vs. Persuasion | KIG](https://kronusintelligencegroup.com/insights/ai-influence-operations-capacity-vs-persuasion): DiResta's October 5 analysis says AI is scaling influence operations, but evidence it changes public opinion is thin. What that means for defending a narrative.
